bull_bear.body:
- Growth has been substantially inorganic on a stated cadence: March 2023 established One Point One USA Inc; February 2024 first acquisition ITCube Solutions Pvt. Ltd.; September 2025 second acquisition ITNITY PTE Ltd; February 2026 third acquisition Netcom BCC.
- Only acquisition consideration disclosed is Netcom BCC at $33.37 Million; the deck gives no funding mix, debt position, dividend policy or balance-sheet detail.
- Commercial model puts fees at risk: the value-differentiator slide states "20% of our fee is at risk on every engagement", while the Governance + Commercial layer states "Up to 30% of fees indexed to client-defined outcome" — the deck carries both figures without reconciling them.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Frames its model against the "Legacy BPM Model": where legacy sells "Headcount as proof of commitment. The bigger the team, bigger the invoice", 1Point1 claims "800 to 8,000 - the team scales with the outcome, not the contract" and "12 consecutive renewals - not because contracts lock clients in, but because outcomes keep them".
- Dual-engine construct: ResolX (1Point1 Technology Labs Pvt Ltd, a wholly-owned subsidiary) "provides the agentic AI and proprietary resolution orchestration - Resolution-as-a-Service", while 1Point1 Solutions "provides the global operations, domain expertise, human judgment and enterprise accountability".
- Four foundational pillars: "Built in Operations, Not in a Lab", "Domain Intelligence That Knows the Workflow", "Accountable for Resolution, Not Activity", and "Enterprise-Grade Global Execution".
- AI positioning rests on owning the stack — "Utility Over Hype", "Zero-Lag Customization" ("Since we own the entire stack"), "Direct Value Transfer" and "Velocity as a Moat" ("deploy modules in days").
- Deck states the company is "Listed in Stock Exchanges" / "Listed on NSE & BSE" and cites "two stock-exchange listings" as part of its right to lead.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Certifications] ISO 42001 (AI management) cited for ResolX; service-suite slide cites ISO 27001/SOC2, "Proven HIPAA / SOC 2 compliance", CENELEC-style claims absent but "Global certifications spanning technology, risk governance, and operational excellence" claimed; uptime cited as "99.97% uptime" and "99.95% uptime" in adjacent tiles.
- [New offering] "Launched Clariva – AI-enabled medical record retrieval process with automated extraction and structuring, humans verifying critical outputs", targeted at the US/North America legal-exposure market.
- [ROI framing] "For every unit of fee, CX clients see 3x-4x of measurable value, validated through sustained annual renewals" — a company claim, not an audited metric.
- [Awards] Recognition listed for 2024–2026 including Best AI/ML Driven Data Center Innovation, Contact Center Excellence Award, AI Leader of the Year (Elets India AI Summit), People First Award, Best Organization for Women Empowerment, and CMD Akshay Chhabra as Most Promising Business Leader of the Year (ET Edge).

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
